# Backlog

Living document — items deferred from earlier sessions plus future ideas with
the reasoning for the deferral. Update when items ship or new ideas land.

## Active themes

### Data foundation (current focus)
Building out player, team, and environmental data coverage so future modeling
work has rich features to draw from. Examples in progress or queued below.

### Daily ops + iteration
Predict → evaluate → improve → export, with incremental fixes as exports surface
issues. Park factors and reliever-as-starter fix shipped recently in this mode.

  >        by a step that runs every morning.

  >    Q6. YES: the placeholder is exempt, by its primary id, in PR-A and in the command's set,
  >        each pinned with a test in which the placeholder holds an NFL membership (527 item 1(7)).

  >        stops the list growing: two clubs on Tuesday, six on Wednesday.

- **What landed:**
  - `IngestionService.sync_teams`, for the college competition ("NCAA") only: before any write for a listed team, the stored team the listing names is resolved by the existing lookup (`_find_team_by_source`, an id a merge recorded included). If it holds a membership of the NFL competition in any season (`_nfl_members`, #1123's set, read once per run) and it is not the placeholder, the listing is refused (`_nfl_member_listed`): no college membership added, no team created, nothing of the team's row written (name, short name, tla, area, founded, venue, external ids). Its provider team id goes on `SyncResult.nfl_member_team_refused` (listing order) and `skipped` counts it once. A team not stored yet holds no membership and goes on as today.
  - The placeholder (545 Q6): the team whose own provider id of the listing's source (`external_ids[source]`, the primary id) is the provider's TBD team (`placeholder.is_placeholder_team`, "345") is never refused, as #1123's refusal and #1119's fill read it.
  - 542 item 1(b), read from the code: sync_teams never deletes a competition_teams row (`_link_team_to_competition` only adds); a refused team's stored college membership stays, every column unchanged, pinned.
  - The line: `nfl_member_team_refused N: <provider team id>, ...` (service.nfl_member_team_refused_line), printed plainly by sync-teams on its own line right after the `✓ Teams (CODE): ...` summary, only when N > 0; sync_teams' log line carries it too.
  - Readers: the admin job's sync-teams summary (` · nfl_member_team_refused N: ...`); sp_run `NFL_MEMBER_TEAM_REFUSED_LINE`, in `_SYNC_LINES`, and `sync_counts` key `nfl_member_team_refused` {n, ids}, every such line of a step adding; laptop_routine `_COUNT_LINES`, so step 8 (NCAA sync-teams) echoes it and its receipt carries it. TEAMS_LINE and every existing reader unchanged.
  - Outside the college competition nothing changes and no query runs; a college run with no NFL member stored looks each listing up once, as before.

NCAA has no model: no prediction output changes, no gate applies.

  - The refusal also holds on a sync-teams run with no `--season`: such a run links nothing but writes the team's row, and 542 1(a) says the row is not touched.

The console never calls it re-dated as a fact (its head reads "not accounted for by the run record"); the result keys `redated_findings` / `REDATED` keep their names, which state no re-dating.

A game the run record accounts for (a window member, or a game its loop reached that took no slot) is after the opening only in a LATER second (re-dated past the opening's second): a member still in the opening's second is never after it, whatever its id (the verification's case: the 59th member 2700 at +200 ms, the 60th 2059 at +500 ms, the opening (that second, 2059); before this, 2700 landed in the members after the opening and Q3 refused permanently although nobody re-dated it). Every other game by its place (`leagues_window.place`): in the opening's second with a higher id it is after the opening, with a lower or equal id before it. At whole-second kickoffs nothing changes; the window's own read (no opening) is byte-identical. In the confirmation's read a ruled item's kickoff (to the second, with the Z) is compared with the game's kickoff cut to the second (`apply_ruled(..., cut=True)`), so an item copied from a refusal matches a sub-second kickoff; the window's read keeps its exact comparison, unchanged (pre-existing).
  - 540 item 1 Q3's order (review P2): a window member now later than the opening is read BEFORE the confirmation's state, in the read and the preflight (`leagues_confirm.moved_refusal`), so a member re-dated to a later second that is not final refuses naming the game and never makes the read WAIT.
  - The guard's "confirmation record" kind pairs the ledger's `confirmation` with its ids file, as "run record" pairs `run` with its file (a design choice). The guard is shared: today nothing holds either kind, so nothing changes; a soccer-expansion-v1 confirmation left on an unmerged laptop branch would refuse that entry's later guard calls until merged; its own `--record` path calls no guard, so 447 C2's PD morning order is unaffected.

  - The confirmation reader goes through no fence: membership() consults none, and a test pins that the fence refuses another reader while the confirmation reads.

- **What landed:**
  - `deploy/hosting/laptop_routine.py`: the daily list (`DAILY`) and its runner, `python deploy/hosting/laptop_routine.py [--weekly] [--dry-run]`. The list is 451 item 3(d) less its step 2, renumbered 1 to 16 in the same order (461 item 2(a)): steps 6 and 7 (NBA, NCAAMB) and 11 (NHL) one day at a time, 14 and 15 two steps each, 6 seconds after each basketball day; 26 commands in all.

  - The refusal comes first: exit 2, nothing resolved, read or run, when `desk_policy.not_laptop_reason()` is not None; the reason is printed (461 item 2(d)). The routine names no fence input, in code or in a string (461 item 2(b)), and never rests on closing's environment-first reading (461 item 2(c)). A real run's refusal writes one receipt (`refused: not_laptop_reason`, the reason beside it; its time and run id are resolved after the read, for that receipt alone); a dry run's writes none and resolves nothing, as sp_run's dry runs write none. A read that raises is refused the same way, its error printed and receipted (by its class name alone when redacting it raises too).
  - Each step runs as `sys.executable cli.py ...` from the checkout, in order. A failing step never stops the next, and none is retried. The step's output streams indented; then one line per step (number, command, exit, seconds), and a sync step's own count, orientation, refusal, collision, skipped-listing and held lines under it (a sync: every `sync-` command, and `nhl-goalie-sync`, step 13, whose `  counts:`, `REFUSED game` and `not in our DB` lines are echoed). A non-zero step also prints its last output line. Last line: steps run, steps failed (a non-zero exit, a timed-out step and a step that could not start; the last two with exit null), non-zero exits, steps timed out and steps not started, routine exits apart.
  - The per-step timeout (461 item 3(a)): each entry carries its limit (`Step.limit_s`), a module constant: `DAILY_STEP_LIMIT` = 1200 and `WEEKLY_LINE_LIMIT` = 2400, for 461's "1,200 for a daily step (each single-day sync counts as its own step), 2,400 for each line of the weekly pass". The limit is each command's, as built, ruled by addendum 469 item 5(1): each of a weekly line's two commands gets its own 2,400 s, and each command of daily steps 14 and 15 (451's 15 and 16) its own 1,200 s. At the limit the child gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after `KILL_GRACE` = 10 s. The step's line and receipt say "timed out after N s", its exit is null, it counts as a failed step, and the next step runs. The routine keeps its own Popen loop: a reader thread streams the output while the main thread waits out the limit. After a clean exit, the reader is waited for as long as it is still reading, so a sync's last count line is kept. After a timeout, it is waited for the kill grace at most: a descendant that outlived the kill and keeps writing never holds the morning a further limit, and the step is also marked `output not drained`. A reader that reads nothing for the grace (a pipe held open) is left, silent; the step is then marked `output not drained`. The routine's own error while reading is marked `output not read` and the pipe is still drained, so it never reads as a timeout. Either keeps the child's exit, is named on the step's line and receipt (`output_error`), and makes the run exit 1: such a step is unreceipted in 461 item 3(d)'s sense (addendum 469 item 5(2)). No environment variable or option sets a limit; `run()` takes an override for the tests alone.
  - The exits (461 item 3(d)): 0 when every step is clean, or its exit is one the list marks routine, and every receipt is written; 1 when a step failed, timed out, could not start or went unreceipted (a step whose output is not whole included, by addendum 469 item 5(2)); 2 for the refusal, nothing run.

Its one `SystemExit(2)` is for `LegacySoccerImproveRefused`, which `training.improve` raises for soccer only. So no step carries a routine exit, and every non-zero exit counts as one. The marking (`Step.routine`) and its separate count are built and tested.
  - Receipts go through `sp_common.append_receipt` unchanged: one per step (kind `step`, unit `laptop-routine`, the shape bootstrap.py uses for its own steps) and one for the run (kind `laptop_routine`, never `chain`). A step that could not start is receipted with exit null (no exit invented) and `not_started` naming why; a step that timed out with exit null, `timed_out`, `limit_s` and `ended_by` (SIGTERM or SIGKILL). Every error the module redacts goes through one helper, `_redacted`: a receipt write, the role read, the weekly list's refusal, a step that cannot start and a read error each fall back to the error's class name alone when redacting raises too (sp_common.redact reads the checkout's `.env`, and one that is not UTF-8 raises), so no error path raises and the refusal stays exit 2. A receipt that cannot be written is printed (`receipt NOT written: ...`) and the run goes on to the next step; the run receipt lists those steps, the last line counts them, and the run exits 1 (461 item 3(c): as built).
  - `--weekly`: the list is read with `readonly_scope` (mode=ro, never created) and printed. Per line, `sync-teams` then `sync-matches`, 6 s after each, inserted before step 8 (NCAA's `sync-teams`, 451's step 9). An unreadable list refuses the run (exit 2). No competition is added by name; FAC 2026/27 stays in the architect's block (461 item 3(b): as built).

  - sp_run.py, sp_backup.py and chains.py are unchanged. No pin is widened and neither pinned test is touched (461 item 2).

**2026-11-14 — The availability graph's node shape: each assertion a node (addendum 379 item 2); ten times today's record builds inside the unit's 1536M (#1007, carrying #995).**
- **Ruling (379 item 2, verbatim in part):** "THE THREE-TIMES CHOICE (#995) — RULED: (B), AND NOT AS AN EXPERIMENT. THE GRAPH'S SHAPE CHANGES: EACH ASSERTION IS A NODE. This amends addendum 252 item 4's 'an edge per assertion'. MemoryMax stays 1536M; (A) is declined: a larger limit on a host with no swap only moves the night it fails."
- **The shape:** `Assertion` nodes carry FACT's properties unchanged. `NAMES_PLAYER`, `NAMES_TEAM` and `ASSERTED_IN` are property-less, forward-only edges from each assertion. The line names the record's assertions beside the graph's assertion nodes, and a build fails if they differ.
- **What the ten-times measurement found:** ten times today's was killed by MemoryMax under the node shape's first load. Three causes, each measured and each found in the engine's v0.22.3 source:
  1. **The record's walk** holds 888 MiB of heap at ten times today's.
  2. **A node checkpoint** that rewrites a string segment leaves its de-duplication table on the heap until a close.
  3. **A relationship COPY into a non-empty table** builds a CSR index for every node group of the assertions, about 8 MiB a group.
- **The load as built:**
  - the walk in a forked child, with SIGTERM blocked across the fork;
  - the nodes in COPYs of 100,000 rows, with the database reopened every 10 and between tables;
  - each relationship table in one COPY into the empty table;
  - the pool a sixth of the limit, 256 MiB.
- **Receipts inside 1536M:**

  | Size | Seconds | Process peak RSS |
  |---|---|---|
  | Today's | 118.7 | 436 MiB |
  | Three times | 380.1 | 589 MiB |
  | Ten times | 1577.2 | 920 MiB |

  What still grows with the record is the walk's longest partition.
- **#995:** carried by #1007. The 11-25 step stands: the architect's block enables on a build, on whichever shape the tag before it carries.

- **Ruling, item 3 (verbatim):** "RULED: the unit changes, the fence does not. "InaccessiblePaths=/etc/sports-predictor" and data/ joins TemporaryFileSystem as ":ro", exactly the two lines the probe ran. Inside this unit the fence then walks an empty folder; that is accepted HERE AND ONLY HERE, because the live file is not in the unit's view at all, the copy is taken only with a matching sha256 sidecar that sp_backup wrote, the open is mode=ro with immutable=1, and ProtectSystem=strict leaves no write path outside the graph's folder. Not one line of check_db loosens for it."
- **Fault one (#996):** the unit's two lines, its header in those terms, and a test that no unit running the app puts a fenced data/ on InaccessiblePaths.
- **Fault two (#996):** the engine's pool is half the limit the rebuild runs under, capped at the unit's MemoryMax, so 768 MiB under the unit. `auto_checkpoint` is ON. The line carries the staged size, the limit and the pool before the load starts.
- **Finding (#995, `class:limitation`, `needs-ruling`):** from the engine's own v0.22.3 source:
  - every COPY forces a checkpoint;
  - every Player sits in one 2^17-node group, which the checkpoint rewrites in memory, unspilled.

  So the pool a FACT checkpoint needs grows with the record. Measured on synthetic records inside 1536M: 1× builds at the rule's 768 MiB; the last COPY that still built reached about 3.2–3.5M FACT edges (2.4–2.6×); 3× fails at every pool from 256 to 1024 MiB.
- **The choice, for the architect:**
  - **(A) A larger MemoryMax:** 2560M builds 3× in 565.6 s, RSS 1813 MiB, on a host with 3,381 MB available and no swap.
  - **(B) Assertions as nodes:** 3× builds at a 256 MiB pool in about 117 s, but it changes 252 item 4's ruled shape.

  The limit is not raised (item 4(b)).
- **/dev/shm (addenda 379 item 3 and 380):** the pre-PR pass reported that systemd's PrivateDevices binds the host's /dev/shm, writable, into the unit.
  - **The host's answer (380 item 1, quoted):** "a file written from inside is PRESENT in the host /dev/shm (the write crossed out of the sandbox)"; with /dev/shm:ro, "absent from the host /dev/shm".

  > 2. THE LAYER'S RULES, standing from today (the page he approved, in my words here; quote these in the records). (a) TWO TIERS, NEVER ONE TABLE: tier api is a fact a provider or league endpoint serves; tier inferred is a stamped claim derived from public news, with a confidence. Every row carries its tier. An inferred row never overwrites or fills an API field; where an API fact exists for the same question the API fact is used and the inferred row stays as the record to be scored. (b) STATUS WORDS of the inferred tier: projected (our estimate under a declared rule, no source), likely (a source suggests it), stated (a source says it outright); each row with its evidence links, the publication time each source showed, the fetch time, the model and prompt version. Append-only: a change of mind is a new row. (c) TWO CLASSES: a TRACKED ELEMENT has a truth that arrives later and is scored on every row; a CONTEXT NOTE is anything else, never scored, never a model input, labelled as reading. A note becomes an element only by promotion from a candidate register (its definition, the truth that scores it, its free baseline), reviewed by me monthly and approved by the operator. (d) SCORED AND GATED: by element, by status, by lead time, with calibration, against the best free baseline (the API layer's own listing where one exists; "the same as last game"). The sample and the margin are written before the first row is stored and do not move. An element that passes may be DECLARED as an input to a candidate, which then runs at that sport's UNCHANGED gate. (e) FORWARD-ONLY: no season is backfilled by an LLM. (f) NO MARKET CONTENT in what the reader is given: no odds, lines or betting articles (the market is a reference, never a model feature). (g) UNKNOWN STAYS UNKNOWN: no evidence, no row. (h) STORED, NEVER REGENERATED: a new model or prompt version starts a new scored series. (i) EACH SOURCE'S TERMS ARE READ BEFORE ITS FIRST FETCH, by a terms phase as the NBA probe has; facts kept, text not republished; one fetch per page per run; on an objection the source is unplugged and its rows destroyed. (j) EVERY PART IS A PLUG. (k) PASS STAYS PASS: nothing inferred changes a call or a stake before its gates.

**2026-11-10 — BUILT (ARCHITECT 2026-11-10 13:05 ET, addendum 321 item 2; addendum 250 item 3; #826 step 1c): the bulletin hooks — the closing run and the slate stage call `cli.py bulletin` on their kept file before their own mirror push; a failure or refusal is receipted (`bulletin_failed` / `bulletin_refused`) and notified as a closing-file failure is, `rec["exit"]` never changed, the push proceeds.**
- **Decision record (ruling, verbatim, addendum 321 item 2):** "THE HOOKS PR (step 1c) — OPEN IT, as #894's body item 1 shaped it: (i) in the closing run, between write_closing_file's success and push_mirror(); (ii) in the slate stage, between link_slate_file's success and push_mirror("slate"); each a subprocess of the command under a try; a failure or refusal receipted bulletin_failed / bulletin_refused and notified as a closing-file failure is; rec["exit"] never changed; the push proceeds with or without the pair; the laptop's MLB closing takes the same hook under laptop/bulletins/; test 6(e) with them; the console's URL lines unchanged. No timer and no chain step of its own: the hooks ride the closing and slate runs that exist."
- **As built:** `closing.bulletin_hook` (one helper, both hooks) runs the command as a subprocess of this checkout in the closing's checkout with `--out-dir exports/bulletins` (the renderer's own default, named so the pairs land where the run's push reads; a test pins `closing.BULLETIN_OUT_DIR` to `bulletin.OUT_DIR`), bounded at 90 s, in its own session (a render still running is killed with its whole process group: `bulletin_failed`; one that exited by the bound keeps its exit, whatever it left behind killed). Exit 2 is `bulletin_refused` only with the render's `BULLETIN REFUSED` verdict line; an exit 2 without it (a broken checkout, a usage error) is `bulletin_failed`. The receipt's `bulletin` names the command, the exit, the seconds and the redacted tail. The MLB laptop path needs no code of its own: `push_mirror` passes the machine's role and `exports_mirror.bulletin_plan` maps `exports/bulletins/<rel>` to `<role>/bulletins/<rel>` (laptop/bulletins/ on the laptop; a test reads the plan).
- **Review before opening (adversarial, two lenses, each finding refute-verified):** three confirmed and fixed: an exit 2 that was not the guard read as REFUSED; a process left holding the output pipe turned an exit-0 render into a timeout and outlived the hook; no test pinned the hook's outer guard (a re-raise there left every test green, and a raising notice would have stopped the push). One refuted: a replaced page's earlier pairs staying in the mirror is ruled design (addendum 250 item 4: the subtree is never pruned), and each pair names its own run id. One noted, not changed: the render's matplotlib writes its font cache under the unit user's home (~/.cache/matplotlib), as it already does on main; nothing is written under data/.
- **Receipts:** tests/test_bulletin_hooks.py 21 passed on 3.10 and 3.12 (each review fix's test fails on its mutant) (6(e): the real render writes the pair before the push; a real render failure leaves exit 0 with `bulletin_failed` receipted, notified, pushed, not run again); the closing, closing-file, slate and bulletin suites unchanged and green on both.

**2026-11-09 — BUILT (ARCHITECT 2026-11-09 16:50 ET, addendum 315 item 2; #865): the Cockpit's store and loader fixes, Codex's five findings on #909 (the v2 loader and store, live on v37). v38 is republished from main after this merges.**
- **Ruling (verbatim, addendum 315 item 2):** "#909 — RULED: MERGE NOW as the faithful sync of v37 plus the 214 port and 305's labels (CI green, clean; 309 item 5's fence stands: the five findings are in code this PR did not write). Codex's five findings are REAL and are MINE — they are live on the published Cockpit today; I built the v2 loader and store in one pass and Codex read what I missed. The ledger is money-path, so the P1s decide the REPUBLISH, not the sync: v38 is republished from main only after the fix PR below merges; until then the live page stays v37 and the operator runs under the interim rules I give him directly (one browser for ledger edits; wait for the "store: … saved" line before importing a CSV or logging a call; no closing the tab within a few seconds of an edit; a partial mirror load is reloaded, never acted on).
   THE FIX PR (Code; ONE PR on tools/cockpit.html; the Cockpit's own tests; first Cockpit slot; Refs #865 and the five threads, each answered with the PR):
   (a) STALE SESSIONS — the ledger carries `rev` (an integer, +1 on every saveLedger) and `updated_at`; the store's header records `rev`; a store write first reads the header: if the header's rev is not the rev this page loaded or last wrote, the page RELOADS the store, MERGES by id (calls by id, fills by id, the newer `updated_at` per record wins; never a silent drop), re-renders, then writes with rev+1.
   (b) EDITS BEFORE LOAD — while the store is loading, saveLedger queues (the local copy still saves); when the load lands, the queued local state is merged into the stored one by the same id-merge and written; the Ledger header says "store: loading… (N edits queued)".
   (c) UNLOAD — `pagehide` and `visibilitychange: hidden` flush the pending write at once (no debounce); and on load the store never overwrites a NEWER local copy: if local.rev > stored.rev, the local copy is written up (the id-merge first), else the store wins — the current one-way rule becomes rev-ordered.
   (d) PARTIAL MIRROR LOAD — the connector loader acts only when EVERY listed file read and parsed; on any failure it keeps the current slate, claims nothing, and prints which files failed with a "Load the N that read" button that the operator presses knowingly (the note then says "PARTIAL" in the summary line).
   (e) CHUNK WRITES (P2) — chunks are written under the new rev's ids (`ledger_chunks/<rev>_<i>`), the header switches to that rev only after every chunk succeeded, and the previous rev's chunks are deleted after the switch (a failed write leaves the old rev intact and readable).
   Tests: the repo copy's test harness for the Cockpit exercises each with a stubbed `claude.use("db")` and `claude.use("mcp")` (two tabs racing; an edit during load; a hidden-page flush; a 13-file listing with one failing read; a chunk write failing at chunk 2). The PR body carries the sha256 of the result; after its merge I diff main's file against v37 (expecting #909's port + these five) and republish as v38 — the repo copy is the source from v38 on, as 309 item 5 has it.
   Under the stop rule these are not #909's rounds (code it did not change; 309 item 5); they are the fix PR's own first review."
- **Built:** as the CHANGELOG fragment lists, (a)-(e), in the store section and ghLoadFolder only.
- **Beyond the ruling's text, for the architect:** (1) chunk ids carry a writer token (`ledger_chunks/<rev>_<i>_<writer>`, not `<rev>_<i>`): two writers that read one header both write the same rev, and with the literal ids a failed write could leave the header naming a mix of the two (a reviewer's blocking repro); the reader takes a chunk only when its rev, index and writer match the header's. (2) The stale check compares the header's rev AND writer, and the write re-reads the header before and after its switch (up to three tries, then "NOT SAVED", and the next save merges again). (3) When the store wins on load, the local records it lacks are set aside (`bd_ledger_v1_set_aside`, counted in the note), not dropped; a merge whose save collapses two calls under the page's unchanged rule (better(): graded first, then the earliest capture) names it and sets the dropped copy aside. (4) A header that does not read whole twice is written over under a new rev, its chunks kept unread; a db read error writes nothing. (5) A localStorage journal of chunk sets lets a later save sweep chunks a closed page left. (6) scripts/cockpit_leg_audit_verify.py strips `updated_at` with the other marks.
- **Open:** the token fallback loader (`loadLatestFromHost`, the F2.5 box) still loads a partial set (item 2(d) names the connector loader); the db offers no compare-and-set, so a header write can still land between another tab's pre-switch check and its write (repaired on that tab's next write or retry, its record otherwise set aside on reopen).
- **Addendum 316 item 1, verbatim:** "#911, item 1 (P1, the header-switch race) — OPTION (a): the runtime HAS the primitive. `DocumentReference.acquire({holder, ttlMs})` is a cooperative lease on a document (db.d.ts: "set-if-not-busy, the single-writer primitive … Busy resolves {acquired:false}, a normal outcome; leases expire on their own; prefer short ttlMs and renew while working"). The store write becomes: acquire the lease on `cockpit/ledger` (holder = this tab's id, a random string made once per page load; ttlMs 10000) → on `{acquired:true}`: read the header, merge by id if its rev is not the one this page holds, write the new rev's chunks, switch the header, then ONE re-read of the header to confirm the switch landed (the belt to the lease's braces; if it moved anyway — a writer not using acquire — merge again on the next save, never drop); on `{acquired:false}`: do not write; retry after `expiresAt` or 2 s, whichever is sooner, up to 5 times, the Ledger header reading "store: busy (another tab is saving), retrying…"; after the fifth, keep the local copy, say "store: NOT saved — another tab holds the store; try again", and leave the pending flag set so the next edit retries. The lease is coordination, not security (the doc says so), and every writer here is this page, so it is enough. The rev stays as the merge key; the lease is the writer lock.
   Item 2 (P1, set-aside) — APPROVED as proposed: records count as set aside only after the set-aside write returns; on failure they stay in the ledger and the note reads "SET-ASIDE FAILED (browser storage full) — N records kept in the ledger"; nothing is reported kept that was not written.
   Item 3 (P2, the stale partial-load button) — BLOCKS, fixed in the same push: each mirror load takes a sequence number; only the latest load may set the note, the button or the slate; an older load that finishes later prints nothing and claims nothing.
   One push carrying the three, with tests (two tabs contending for the lease, one busy; a set-aside write that throws; two overlapping loads finishing out of order); then green CI → my merge block → I diff main's tools/cockpit.html against v37 and republish as v38 (the first republish since the sync; the repo copy is the source).
   On the stop rule: this is the ruled fix of a second-round P1 on money path, which the rule allows (every P1 has a fix or a ruling); the P2 is included by my word, not as a round."
- **Built (316 item 1, the ruled fix of Codex's second review):** (1) every store write runs under `cockpit/ledger`'s lease (`acquire({holder, ttlMs: 10000})`; the runtime has no release verb, so a lease lapses 10 s after its last grant, and a long write renews it); a busy lease writes nothing, retries after expiresAt or 2 s (whichever is sooner) up to 5 times, then says NOT saved and keeps the pending flag (kept in the browser too, so a page closed under a busy lease merges on reopen); one re-read of the header after the switch. (2) A set-aside counts only after its write returns; on a failure the records stay in the ledger ("SET-ASIDE FAILED (browser storage full) — N records kept in the ledger"), and a store write is built from the page's own last save when the browser refused the local copy (an older copy never reaches the store). (3) Each mirror load takes a sequence number; only the latest sets the note, the button or the slate.

**2026-11-09 — BUILT (ARCHITECT 2026-11-09, addendum 310 items 3, 4 and 5; incident #902): THE PROVIDER ID IS THE SEASON'S. For every source that is not SPORT_WIDE, the upsert's provider-id lookup is scoped to the competition AND the listed row's own season; the prefetch cache keys (id, season) and stays O(1). A stored row of another season carrying the listed id is never touched: the listing creates its own row, and the sync prints `provider_id_collision N: <stored id> (<season>) ← <listing id>`. The re-key index (pairs, `_prev`, the placeholder window) is the season's. The orientation chain is unchanged in code; its docstring gains 3(e)'s line. The restore script ships here; the architect's block runs it after the fix is on main. The HOLD of item 2 stands until then. Refs #902.**

Today the SAME row ids with the SAME provider ids read season 2026, 2026-10-31 19:45Z Utah v Cincinnati and 2026-11-07 20:30Z Alabama v LSU. v1r's 762-id 2025 test set reads 762 × 2025 on 10-09 and 760 × 2025 + 2 × 2026 today. - **Ruling (verbatim, addendum 310 item 1):** "THE MECHANISM (service.py:547, read): the upsert's id lookup is `Match.competition_id == comp.id` for every source but mlb_stats_api — ANY season. The provider served ids 18216 and 18240 on the 2026 editions of two annual games (Utah–Cincinnati, Alabama–LSU); the 2026 listing found the 2025 rows by id and `_upsert_match` rewrote season, kickoff, status and scores onto them. Because each annual game swaps venue, the listing's home/away was the stored pair reversed — THAT is what the orientation chain read on 11-07/08 and "repaired" by writing the 2026 scores into the stored (2025) orientation. The chain did what it was built to do; what it was built on was wrong: the two cases were id collisions, not reversed listings. Consequences today: two 2025 games are gone from the pot; the two 2026 games sit on rows whose home/away is the 2025 venue (Utah home, Alabama home — both wrong for 2026), with Kalshi odds_snapshots and the orientation receipt attached to those ids; v1r's record is unreproducible on 2 of 762 until the restore; v2's FAIL does not move (its inputs were the 2026 scores, which are right by team)."

BACKLOG decision record, CHANGELOG fragment, Refs #902. Nothing else in the PR."

**2026-11-09 — BUILT (ARCHITECT 2026-11-09 10:05 ET, addendum 305, money path, a tightening): a PLAY whose executable edge is zero or negative is a PASS, pass_kind `exec_non_positive`. The Desk never buys above its own price. No date moves; no bar moves.**
- **The finding (verbatim, in part):** "A DESK POLICY GAP, found by the operator's NFL audit and CONFIRMED in desk_policy.py — a PLAY whose EXECUTABLE edge is zero or negative is still emitted at half units. [...] Sunday's Bears would-be (model 73.2%, all-in 73.4¢, exec −0.2pp, "exec < 4pp half units") is the instance. The renderer's own text (constants, `pp`/`cents`/`pct`, the parsed kickoff's ET and UTC stamps, the stage line) is not escaped; the card is a PNG and draws plain text, unescaped, its strings read by the guard as before. The credential pattern lets `_ * ~` join and close a label's words ("api _key_ = …", "*api key*: …": the field displays its delimiters, and reads as a credential): a tightening of the shape the field-level scan refuses, not a rendering normalization. Tests: a walk over every string the SOCCER, NFL and MLB rows carry (each a token holding `<`, `_` and `*`; none printed unescaped, no `<` in the Markdown); an unclassified field refused; eleven forms (link, image, nested parentheses, long tag, long comment, processing instruction, declaration, CDATA, underscore and asterisk emphasis, spaced label) each refused at the field as `secret` with a credential shape and written as literal text without one; a golden render read back as its field values; the existing tests compare the displayed text (a `displayed()` helper reverses only the escapes). The duplicate target-path P2 and the concurrent-run temp P2 stay on #896 (item 2(e)). THE RECORD (item 2): "six real findings in five rounds is the cost of normalizing a renderer we do not own; escaping is the rule for every future publisher of free text to a rendered surface (bulletins today; anything that writes Markdown to GitHub tomorrow)."
- **The pre-push review of the escaping (a495cc5a; rendered with cmark-gfm, GitHub's renderer), fixed before the push:** (1) a value that opens a list item's content could open block markup: four leading spaces an indented code block (the escapes then shown as backslashes), `1. FC Köln` an ordered list, `- `/`+ ` a nested list, `---` a rule: `md_escape` also backslash-escapes `- + = .` and writes leading and trailing spaces as `&#32;`; (2) GFM's extended autolinks took `https://…` and `www.…` as links with the escapes inside them: `md_escape` also escapes `:` (and `.`), which stops both; (3) a host.env key wrapped in `<…>`, a link target or a comment was written as an escaped `\[REDACTED\]` (the rendered readings dropped the key): `field_offence` refuses as `secret` any value `sp_common.redact` would change, as 298 B item 5 rules; (4) a team name ending in a label beside a token-shaped ticker displays `…api_key: <token>` that neither field holds: the guard also reads the whole document as GitHub displays it (`display_text`, the exact inverse of the escaping: one reading of our own output, not a re-implementation of GitHub's); (5) the walking test covers the whole document (rows, `desk_meta` and its rules, the closing block, the day's slate row and file name, the certification text), and a raw interpolation of any of them fails it (each mutation checked); (6) `_EMPH` is bounded to three characters (an unbounded run backtracked into the token's lookahead, quadratic). Beyond the ruled escape list, therefore: `- + = . :` and the edge spaces, each escaped the CommonMark way so it displays as itself. The second pre-push review (0cff8033): an empty value is written as `&#32;` (a bare `  - ` under the reason line read as a setext underline and made the line a heading). Residual, for the architect: GitHub links an e-mail address and an `xmpp:` address after the escapes are read (the same autolink pass; its text is the value, character for character); GitHub's emoji shortcodes (`:name:`) are a post-render filter no Markdown escape reaches; and a credential split across two list items with `:` or `=` opening the second ("api key" / ": abcdef123") is not refused, as at 0de9bdd0 (the displayed text keeps the list marker between them; refusing it would be a new normalization of a reading, which 319 item 2(b) rules out). tests/test_bulletin.py: 240 cases on Python 3.12 (one, the cmark-gfm render of every finding form, skips where cmark-gfm is not installed, as on CI).

- **Ruling (verbatim, addendum 288 item 1):** "THE KICKOFF, RULED (286 item 4(a); THE TIMES): occurrence_datetime is served on 1,362 of 1,372 ATP markets and sits +7 h to +29 h after 00:00 UTC of the ticker's date — the ticker's date is the US-Eastern calendar day of the start (02:00–24:00 ET), and expected_expiration_time carries the same instant on every market (the same offset table); open_time is the day before (−4 to −20 h), close_time about two weeks later (the venue's reschedule window). The 24 active ATP and 6 active WTA markets of 11-08 all carry an occurrence_datetime later today (14:00Z, 15:30Z, 17:00Z, 19:30Z; WTA 16:00Z, 23:00Z, 00:30Z 11-09) and were all refused as in play by the stored UTC+14 rule — the receipt shows the cost 286 item 4(a) named, exactly. RULED: a tennis row's kickoff = the event's occurrence_datetime, as served, UTC; both markets of the event must carry the same value (a difference refuses the event with its own label, counted); absent on both → expected_expiration_time by the same rule; absent on all four → the row is stored with the conservative UTC+14 instant AND the label START_UNREAD, so it is never captured and the receipt counts it. The stored kickoff is re-read on every sync (a postponed match's market "will remain open and close after the rescheduled match has finished (within two weeks)" — the venue's own words below — so the instant moves and the row follows it). The coverage day is the ET day of the kickoff, which is the ticker's date; the shared matcher's date-only rule therefore reads the right row; the IN_PLAY refusal fires at the real start. The chain's three ticker days at 06:53Z now write rows whose kickoffs lie ahead."
- **Ruling (verbatim, addendum 288 item 2(a)-(c)):** "(a) the map does NOT change on this addendum; the 106 stay SCHEDULED and labelled, which is law 4 working"; "(b) the receipt gains, in the follow-up PR, a line per distinct expiration_value SHAPE on the unmapped events (the value verbatim, the count, the 'yes' player beside it for three samples) and the served phase is re-run by my block"; "(c) the ruling on the map follows that read — the likely shape of it, written now so the read can confirm or refute it: on two finalized markets whose result words are 'yes' and 'no', the result words name the winner (the 'yes' market's player) and expiration_value is recorded verbatim beside it; an expiration_value that names the OTHER player is a contradiction and refuses the event, counted; a token or an empty value refuses nothing. Nothing of (c) is built before the read."
- **Ruling (verbatim, addendum 288 item 3):** "THE CONTRACT CLAUSE, quoted from rules_secondary (686 distinct values, one sentence common to every market; CONTRACT_TERMS_QUOTE fills from this): "If the match does not occur (signaled by a ball being played) due to a player injury, walkover, forfeiture, or any other cancellation (all before the match starts), the market will resolve to a fair price in accordance with the rules. If this match is postponed or delayed, the market will remain open and close after the rescheduled match has finished (within two weeks)." And rules_primary: "If <player> wins the <A> vs <B> professional tennis match in the <event> after a ball has been played, then the market resolves to Yes." early_close_condition on every market: "This market will close and expire after a winner is declared." THE MEANING, recorded: SETTLED_SCALAR = the match did not occur (injury, walkover, forfeiture or cancellation before a ball was played) and the venue settled at "a fair price" — 20 ATP and the WTA scalar events, the fractions kept verbatim; a retirement AFTER a ball is played produces a yes/no settlement, the advancing player the winner — FINISHED, as built (287's reading confirmed by the venue's words); the status word's docstring carries this sentence and the quote. contract_terms_url is the venue's generic "ACHIEVEMENTS.pdf" for both series — the per-market rules are the terms that bind, and they are now on the record."
- **Ruling (verbatim, addendum 288 item 5):** "THE KICKOFF FOLLOW-UP PR (Code, a code slot, money-path; the retraction fix of 287 item 2 rides with it): (a) item 1's kickoff rule with its labels and tests (the four cases); (b) the retraction fix (an incoming unsettled or changed result clears full_time_result and returns the row to its served state); (c) item 2(b)'s receipt line (read-only); (d) item 3's quote and meaning in the status word's docstring and the adapter's CONTRACT_TERMS_QUOTE; (e) NOT the map change of item 2(c) — a second small push after my read of the re-run receipt, if the read confirms it. - **Built:** `kalshi_tennis.kickoff` / `read_instant` and the kickoff labels (`START_UNREAD`, `OCCURRENCE_DIFFER`, `EXPIRATION_DIFFER`, `OCCURRENCE_ONE_MARKET`, `EXPIRATION_ONE_MARKET`, `OCCURRENCE_UNREAD`, `EXPIRATION_UNREAD`), `Fixture.kickoff` / `kickoff_source`, `Listing.kickoff_sources`; `NormalizedMatch.kickoff_source` stored as `external_ids["kalshi_kickoff"]` (no schema change); `tennis_kalshi.kickoff_check` (`START_UNREAD_ROW`, `KICKOFF_SOURCE_MISSING`); `tennis_kalshi.served_kickoff_check` (the kickoff rule read again over the event's open markets at capture: `KICKOFF_REFUSED_NOW`, `KICKOFF_UNREAD_NOW`, `KICKOFF_MOVED`, `KICKOFF_HELD_NOT_TWO`); `service.SERVED_STATE_SOURCES` (the retraction fix, tennis only); the receipt's SHAPES line, THE TIMES as ruled and the stored kickoff sources; `CONTRACT_TERMS_QUOTE` and `SETTLED_SCALAR`'s meaning.
- **Decided conservatively, put to the architect (PR body):** a key served on one market only refuses the event (never the next key); a served value that is no ISO instant with an offset refuses it; a JSON null or blank string is not served; two spellings of one instant are one value; a row with no stored kickoff source is never captured; at capture, a served start that is not the row's stored kickoff, or one market of the event in hand, refuses the placement. Open: whether a refused event's stored row (its last status, winner and settlement receipt kept) is changed on the sync.
- **Finding (the rule unchanged):** at the top of the ruled range the served kickoff's US Eastern day is D+1, not the ticker's date (+29 h in EST, +28 h and +29 h in EDT; "24:00 ET" is 00:00 of D+1): the coverage page reads that row on D+1; the shared matcher still places the event on its one row, and refuses it (DATE_TIE / TWO_ROWS) where the same pair holds a row of D+1.
- **Reachability (not widened):** the retraction fix is reached for a row re-served inside the chain's ticker window or by the late re-read, which reads stored SCHEDULED rows only, 7 ticker days back; a FINISHED or SETTLED_SCALAR row whose ticker day has left the window is not re-read (Codex on #868, cli.py:310).

- **As built:** `exports_mirror.bulletin_plan` walks `exports/bulletins/`; every regular `.md` / `.png` goes to `<role>/bulletins/<the same relative path>` byte for byte, whatever its mtime, nested `<FAMILY>/<date>/` and `<FAMILY>/weeks/` kept as they are. A bulletin removed from `exports/` stays in the mirror, matching the top-level rule, under which a dated copy whose source is gone stays until its folder expires (the push never deletes for a missing source; the subtree never expires).
- **The choice on other files, receipted rather than silent (law 2):** anything under the subtree that is not a regular `.md` / `.png` (a `.json` above all), a symlink anywhere (never followed, the root included), a `.git` path component, an unreadable folder, a kept file the push cannot read (no read permission, or gone since the plan) and a path git itself refuses (git decides, by `add --ignore-errors`; `.git`'s NTFS spellings `GIT~1`, `.git.`, `.git ` under core.protectNTFS, its default) are never copied and are counted: `skipped` (path, reason) on the push's result and `bulletins: N skipped (<reason> <count> · …)` on its console line, which the chain hooks' mirror receipts keep. Silence would let a renderer's stray `.json` (the thing item 4 forbids) go unseen; the count makes it visible on the next morning's receipts. One bad bulletin is local to that file: it never stops the push of the top-level files (nothing under `exports/bulletins/` could before this PR), and a refused copy is removed from the working clone so it never jams a later push. No subtree: nothing happens, no new key.
- **The compare untouched:** `deploy/hosting/compare_exports.py` and `deploy/exports-mirror/compare.yml` are not in the diff; a test pins that the compare's `*.json` glob over a mirror tree holding `bulletins/` (with a `.json` planted in `exports/bulletins/`) finds no bulletin path, that the shipped Action's date pick never takes `bulletins/` (pending on a tree holding only bulletins; CLEAN on the common dated folder), and that the shipped tool on the two `bulletins/` folders compares 0 JSON.
- **Codex on #847, round 1 (P2, verified on 3441675a):** a symlink the mirror's own tree already tracks on a bulletin's destination (the file, a folder above it, `bulletins/`, the role folder; relative escape or absolute) carried the push's write, or git's check's walk and unlink, out of the clone. The destination is now lstat'ed component by component from `<role>/` down and never followed: that bulletin is skipped and receipted (`destination path has a symlink`, `destination path has a non-folder`, `destination not a regular file`), the tracked entry left visible as it is rather than unlinked or overwritten, and the top-level files and the other bulletins still push. A tracked submodule on the path is refused the same way, by the index's gitlink entries (`destination path has a submodule`), and never aborts the push (+11 tests, failing on 3441675a).
- **2026-11-06, addendum 277 item 1 (R2-1, round 2 on #847, BUILT), verbatim:** "R2-1 BLOCKS — BUILD: the mirror publishes ONLY the paths its plan copied. The whole-tree `add -A` is main's mechanism, and it means any stray file in the clone — a leftover of a killed run, a file another writer dropped there — goes to the mirror unplanned; the mirror is private, and the Desk's privacy rules still say nothing leaves a machine that was not planned to. The fix is the add limited to planned paths (never `git clean -fd`: the mirror deletes nothing it did not plan either); a leftover from a killed run is then never published and the next run's receipt names it as untracked-and-skipped. One fix push with its fail-first test; green CI; no new round (the cap); my block on that head." **As built:** `exports_mirror.push` no longer runs a whole-tree `git add -A`: it stages by name (`_stage`: `git add --force --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul`, `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1`) exactly the dated and latest copies, the bulletins it carried (minus the skipped and the refused; `_refused_by_git` now adds those paths only and removes only a refused planned copy, never walking the subtree), `tools/compare_exports.py` and `.github/workflows/compare.yml`; the latest cleanup and the prune go through `git rm` on tracked paths only (`pruned` names the folders that held tracked files); a planned path beyond a symlink or inside a submodule is never staged (the top-level rule's own hole keeps its own Issue and PR); any other untracked file in the working clone is never staged and never deleted (no clean, no unlink) and is named on the result (`untracked_skipped`) and the console line (`untracked-and-skipped N (...)`); the squash commits the index as the sync left it, never a whole-tree add, and names the same files. One existing test's tail changes by the ruling: a refused stray (`bulletins/GIT~1/z.md`) a killed push left behind, its source gone, is now kept and receipted as untracked-and-skipped instead of deleted. **Receipts:** a synthetic probe on fbbd3148 (tmp dirs, a local bare remote, five strays planted untracked in the clone, then a push that commits) published four of them (`host/bulletins/NFL/2026-10-03/stray.json`, `host/bulletins/stray.md`, `host/stray.md`, `stray-root.txt`), deleted the fifth (`host/latest/stray.json`), and its squash published the four; on the fix, 0 published, 5 kept on disk, the squash 0. +4 tests (`test_a_stray_untracked_file_in_the_clone_is_never_published_never_deleted_and_receipted`, `test_a_killed_runs_leftover_is_never_published_and_the_next_run_receipts_it`, `test_the_squash_publishes_only_the_tracked_tree`, `test_the_planned_deletions_remove_tracked_paths_only`), fail-first on fbbd3148's `exports_mirror.py`: 5 failed (the 4 new and the amended one), 35 passed; on the fix: 40 passed. Review of the fix (two findings, verified): (1) the planned-path add followed git's ignore rules, so a stray untracked `.gitignore` at the clone root or under `<role>/`, or a `.git/info/exclude` entry, matching a planned dated, latest or bulletin path made git's add exit 1 and abort the push, and a stray is never deleted, so every later push would abort (fbbd3148's whole-tree add pushed through it, publishing the `.gitignore`, dropping the ignored new files and receipting the bulletin as refused): `_stage` now adds with `--force` (the list is the plan; core.protectNTFS still refuses), the planned files reach the remote, and the stray `.gitignore` stays on disk, unpublished, receipted as untracked-and-skipped; (2) a tracked file the plan does not write, edited by another writer between the sync and the add, is not published (tested) but is not untracked, so it is not on the receipt: the docstring and spec claim is narrowed to untracked files and states the tracked case (race-only; the next sync's `reset --hard` restores it, as on main; the ruling names untracked-and-skipped only, so no new receipt field is built, and one is listed for the follow-up Issue). +2 tests (`test_an_ignore_rule_in_the_clone_never_vetoes_a_planned_path_or_jams_the_push`, three cases: `.gitignore`, `host/.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude`; `test_a_tracked_file_another_writer_edits_after_the_sync_is_never_published`): the file against fbbd3148's `exports_mirror.py` 9 failed, 35 passed; against the fix without `--force` the 3 ignore cases fail (`CalledProcessError`, exit 1), 41 passed; on the final fix 44 passed; the full suite: 5368 passed, 3 skipped, 5 xfailed. R2-2 and R2-3 go to the PR's one follow-up Issue, not built here.

Step 2 (the weekly digest) after step 1 is merged. No roadmap date (item 8).

- **Addendum 252, verbatim (items 1, 2, 6, 7):**

> 1. THE MODEL, bitemporal and append-only. Two tables, both created by one migration, both written by ingest commands only, both read mode=ro by everything else:
>    (a) `availability_observations` — one row per fetch: sport; source (a fixed vocabulary, item 3); endpoint (the URL or file name, no secrets); the match_id where the fetch is per game (NULL for a league-wide file), the stored kickoff then; poll_label where polled on a schedule (the probe's T-120 … T-0); scheduled_at; fetched_at (OUR clock, UTC); http_status; payload_sha256; payload_path (the raw answer kept on disk under logs/availability/<source>/<date>/, never under data/, never mirrored); status: complete | partial | empty | failed | missed (Step B's five, the same meanings); late; error (redacted); rows_asserted. NOTHING UPDATES OR DELETES A ROW. A fetch that raised is a row; a poll whose time passed with no call is a row.
>    (b) `availability_assertions` — one row per fact a payload asserted, keyed to its observation: observation_id; sport; kind (a fixed vocabulary: depth_rank | projected_starter | confirmed_starter | eventual_starter | inactive | injury_status | plays_for); player_id (ours, NULL with the source's id beside it when unmapped: source_player_id, player_name verbatim); team_id (ours; NULL + source_team verbatim when unmapped); match_id (NULL for a team-level fact); attrs JSON (pos_abb, pos_slot, pos_rank, status text, the side); source_stamp (THE SOURCE'S OWN TIME for the fact: nflverse's `dt`; NULL where the source gives none — the NHL landing gives none); recorded_at (= the observation's fetched_at, denormalised for the as-of query). No valid_to column and no update: an interval is DERIVED — a fact holds from its observation to the next observation of the same source that asserts the same (kind, player, team[, match]) differently, or that asserts the slot to someone else. "As of T" is one query: the newest observation per source with the chosen clock <= T, and its assertions. That is StackState's time travel in two tables and a WHERE clause.
>    THE TWO CLOCKS, ruled now so no term argues it later: `recorded_at` is OUR knowledge; `source_stamp` is the source's claim. A live-era record, a forward confirmation and a closing-time input use `recorded_at` only (what we had on our disk before the cut-off). A backfilled row (recorded_at later than source_stamp by more than the feed's cadence: nflverse's season file reaches back to its first load, so our first fetch records weeks of history at once) is usable ONLY in a backtest labelled "source-stamped" in its run record and its gate text, never in the live-era record; a term that wants it declares that in its bar. Both clocks are kept on every row so either reading can be audited.
>    Mapping (law 4): a player or team the source names that we cannot map stays NULL with the source's text beside it; mapping is by the existing tables' source ids (players.gsis_id / espn_id where we hold them, nhl player ids as nhl_goalies stores them) and never by name alone; an unmapped row is counted on the ingest's console and in a receipt, never dropped and never guessed.
>
> 2. THE QUERY SURFACE (read-only cli, one command): `availability --sport S --as-of INSTANT [--clock recorded|source] [--match-id N | --team T] [--kind K]` prints the facts in force at the instant under the chosen clock, each with both stamps and its observation; `--history` prints every assertion for the key in time order so a flip shows. The same function is the one a model term, the bulletin's teams section and the Cockpit will read; there is no second path.
>
> 6. TESTS (the acceptance set): (a) append-only — the ingest commands expose no update or delete path, and a test asserts the tables' row counts only grow across a replay of saved payloads; (b) the as-of query under each clock on a synthetic history with a flip, a backfilled row and a missed poll — the recorded clock never returns the backfilled row before its fetch; (c) the five statuses on saved payloads: complete, partial (a team unmapped), empty, failed (a raised call), missed (a scheduled poll with no call); (d) the nflverse adapter on a saved 2025-format file: every column read by name (law 1), the 2023–2024 shape refused with its reason; (e) the NHL adapter on the probe's saved payloads (the same files the leaders-order receipt reads): leaders[0] per side, two in net, no goalieComparison; (f) a payload with an unmapped player keeps its name and NULL id; (g) the derived interval on a sequence of observations equals the flip the history shows; (h) nothing under data/ after any test.
>
> 7. ORDER AND DATES (a new lane `availability-record` in docs/roadmap.json with these steps; no existing date moves; its Issue filed with the schema PR; the board places it immediately below the model lanes, since the NHL and NFL-QB lanes cannot declare without it — it is the first tooling that unblocks a model lane rather than waits beside one): the schema PR (item 1, the migration, the query command, tests 6(a)–(c), (g), (h)) opens in the next free slot after #825's merge-from-main push and the parity PR — due 11-10; the nflverse feed (3(a), its chain and timer) due 11-12, so the first host observations precede the 11-13 decision; the NHL landing feed (3(b), the watch) due 11-17; the paid adapter, if named, specified 11-14 and due 11-21; the projection's candidate comparison due 11-20, the rebuild due 11-25. The bulletins lane (addendum 250) queues behind the schema and nflverse PRs and ahead of the projection. Each PR body names its commands and arguments; no block ships to the operator; the first host reads and the timers' enablement are my blocks. Thursday's migration tag does not carry any of it.

  - "(3) THE WALK'S FLOOR: the arm's live walk takes an EXPLICIT floor at the gate's warm-up season (`nb.WARMUP_SEASON`, 2024), pinned by a test in which a stored pre-2024 FINISHED NFL game does not enter the arm's walk and is counted on the export's summary line ("walk floor 2024; N stored games before it, excluded"). v1's own walk is NOT changed in this lane (the live row's walk is a v1 question, 230's scope); a pre-2024 finished NFL game appearing in the DB is a data event with its own Issue, never a silent inclusion."
  - "(4) THE TIE RULE: agreed — pinned by text (the test reads the gate's source and asserts the expression) and by value; no refactor of frozen gate code before Friday's run. A refactor to one shared function after the run is optional, its own small PR, and must leave the gate's bytes-as-run reproducible from the tag."
  - "THE CODEX P1 (rounding): the fix is right and is round 1 — the arm stores full precision and rounds only where it is shown (the slate and closing rows, the results row, the summary line, the receipt); the new test fails on the current code and passes on the fix. v1's four-place storage (nfl_predict.py:139) is UNCHANGED: it is the live row and this lane does not touch it. The weekly comparison line names the precision on its own line ("v2 at full precision as stored; v1 at four places as stored; the difference is bounded at about 1e-4 of log-loss") — immaterial against the 0.010 bar and the 7.0pp band, and stated so no reader mistakes it for a divergence."
- **(1) The state is read, never written.** `nfl_rehearsal.read_gate` / `state` read the `nfl-elo-v2` entry at call time. The arm is on only when all of these hold:
  - this is the host;
  - `verdict.verdict == "PASS"`, with its `at` (the architect's record, never the computed run text);
  - `status == "rehearsal"`;
  - `rehearsal_window` is exactly `{"opens_at": "<instant>Z", "closes_at": "<instant>Z"}`, opens before closes;
  - the declared term and the frozen constants price.

  Every other reading is dormant, with its reason. The instants are read from the entry and never defaulted. A test pins 247's ruled `{"opens_at": "2026-11-12T00:00:00Z", "closes_at": "2026-11-24T06:00:00Z"}` and that a different window is followed.

  This PR writes no registry field: the verdict-record PR after Friday writes the state, on PASS only. The real registry reads dormant today.
- **(2) The compare.**
  - The slate and closing rows carry `rehearsal_version`, `rehearsal_probabilities`, `rehearsal_term`, `rehearsal_verdict_stamp`, `rehearsal_label` and `rehearsal_reason`.
  - The results row and the record carry `rehearsal_arm`.
  - compare_exports never compares or prints a `rehearsal_*` key at any depth. It counts them on `rehearsal-arm keys (host-only, nfl-elo-v2): N`, right after the pl-availability line.
  - No `candidate_*` key is used, and the pl-availability line and its count are unchanged.
- **(3) The window opens per game, by kickoff.** The kickoff must fall in [opens_at, closes_at). The week-11 MNF at 2026-11-24T01:15Z is inside, and 06:00Z is outside. A row predicted before the window for a game inside it carries the arm (pinned); a game outside it never does.
- **(4) After the window.**
  - The export writes no new arm row: no covered game is upcoming once closes_at has passed (pinned with a closed window: nothing stored, every file equal to the stubbed code's).
  - On the host, export-nfl-results reads every stored arm, whatever the registry reads later (pinned with the window closed, the status `production`, a FAIL, and no entry).
  - Off the host, nothing is read.
- **(5) Ties and weeks.** Each figure's rule is stated on its line (`record.rehearsal_arm.rules`):
  - The log-loss is walk_protocol's arithmetic: a tie counts as a home loss, and the mean is accumulated as the gate accumulates it. It is pinned equal to `ll_model` to the bit.
  - The Brier is (p - y)^2 on the same y.
  - The W-L-P and vs-close treat a tie as a push.
  - Per week means by the row's `week` (matches.matchday).
- **(6) The live walk.** v1's `_current_ratings` runs under the declared term for the whole walk, from the walk floor (251 item 3(3)). A parity test on the synthetic stream, walked both ways, finds the 2025 probabilities equal to the gate's scored ones, game for game. The arm is stored at full precision, so the stored and graded probabilities are the gate's floats as well (Codex on #825); the pages and the results row's `home_win_prob` / `away_win_prob` present them at four places, and the results row carries the full-precision `p_home` the figures are computed from.
- **(3 of 247) The Desk pin.** Bare, armed and loud docs give byte-identical output for:
  - `desk_meta` and the desk blocks;
  - `closing.desk_rows` (with `would_be_for`);
  - `exec_cohorts.would_be_play`;
  - `closing.page_text`.

  No Desk code names the keys. The arm labels each row with the entry id, the term, the verdict stamp and "rehearsal — not a call". The closing summary block and the run receipt carry one arm line; the phone page carries none, as 223 item 3 placed the would-be line.
- **251 item 3, as built:**
  - **(1) Post-Friday parity.** The gate is unchanged: no per-game dump. `nfl_rehearsal.parity` walks the arm's live walk (`walk`, the floor applied, the declared term for the whole walk) over the record's scored ids (`scored_ids`: the registry IDS_DIR sidecar, count and sha256 checked) and compares the record's own figures: its log-loss (`ll_model`, result_record's key for walk_protocol's figure) to its stored precision, and every band's n, `stated` and `realized` means to six places. On the synthetic stream, recorded by the real `nfl_v2_gate.result_record` and `registry.record_run`, it passes, and it names a mismatch for a walk without the floor, a record one unit off, a band off by 1e-6 and a dropped id. The real-record test is skipped with a named reason (`parity_skip`, asserted by text) until the record exists. Once the record exists, the sidecar's count and sha256 and the record's shape (`record_shape`) are checked everywhere, CI included, and only the walk is skipped when no database copy is given, with its own named reason. A skip is never silent: each reason is also warned (`ParitySkipped`), so the warnings summary of CI's plain `pytest -q` run names it.
  - **(2) The dependency.** The verdict-record PR after Friday carries the five status-aware places with `rehearsal` added and a test over the enum: `registry.record_verdict` (writes `confirming` on a PASS), `registry.record_confirmation` (reads it), coverage_map's lane/registry disagreement check, roadmap STATES, and tests/test_leagues_declaration_220.py's status pin. This PR changes none of them, and the arm stays dormant until the record reads PASS and `status: "rehearsal"`.
  - **(3) The walk's floor.** The arm's live walk passes `floor=nfl_rehearsal.WALK_FLOOR`, which is `nfl_backtest.WARMUP_SEASON` (2024), imported. A stored game of an earlier season is left out of the arm's walk and counted on the predict run's arm line: "walk floor 2024; N stored games before it, excluded". v1's walk passes no floor and is unchanged. A pre-2024 FINISHED NFL game in the DB is a data event with its own Issue, never a silent inclusion. A test stores a FINISHED 2023 game: the arm's probabilities equal an independent walk from 2024, v1's equal one over every stored game, and the line reads "walk floor 2024; 1 stored games before it, excluded".
  - **(4) The tie rule.** Pinned by text (the gate's source: the outcome, the per-game log-loss, the floor, the band index and means) and by value (walk_protocol scores a one-game stream, a tie among the cases, and `game_log_loss` on `gate_y` gives its `ll_model` to the bit). No refactor of the frozen gate's code.
  - **The Codex P1 (rounding), round 1.** The arm is stored at full precision and rounded only where it is shown. v1's four-place storage is unchanged. The record block names the precision on its own line (`rules.precision`), verbatim: "v2 at full precision as stored; v1 at four places as stored; the difference is bounded at about 1e-4 of log-loss".
- No constant, bar, gate threshold, roadmap date or registry value moved. The market is a reference, never a model feature.

The host list's NCAA line is not verified; first or last is the architect's to rule. The read runs only when the list resolves (setting set, file present, a competition listed), the daily backup succeeds and no earlier `sync-matches` fails; in every other case that week's read waits for a hand run or the next Sunday. Widening go_on is not ruled.
- **Statement for the architect (no change made):** each Sunday run is a full non-dry 2026 ingest. It upserts and re-stamps the completed-game labels (`ncaa_cfbd_labels`), appends one ingest record (`ncaa_cfbd_ingest_records`), upserts the pregame rows (`ncaa_cfbd_pregame`, only behind its migration marker) and saves the raw payload under `exports/cfbd/` (not mirrored). The new record becomes 2026's latest, so D6's 2026 coverage fact and L3's current rule (the 2026 labels the gate stream walks, the pregame rows the shadow reads) read that run from then on. The matches table, 2024 and 2025 are untouched. Without `CFBD_API_KEY` in the unit's environment the command refuses with exit 2 before any read; under go_on that is a failed step, and the chain's exit pages. An HTTP 200 with an empty list exits 0 and does not page, yet its 0-record ingest record becomes 2026's latest: every 2026 label and pregame row then reads non-current (L3), D6's 2026 coverage fact reads not covered, and the stream walks no 2026 label until a later non-empty read. A payload missing its required fields also writes such a record, but exits 2 and pages. One GET per run; sp_run retries the step (15s, then 45s; at most 3 reads) only on a timeout, a connection reset or abort, a 429, or a 504 by its `Gateway Timeout` text; a CFBD 500, 502 or 503 is not retried: exit 1, no ingest record, it pages. Whichever is later, a Sunday read or item (a)'s hand run, becomes 2026's latest record; a CFBD read between the v2 `--preflight` and the run that adds, drops or changes a walked 2026 label (a week's newly completed games do) changes the stream's fingerprint, and the run then refuses on the mismatch; `fetched_at` is not a fingerprint field, so a re-read that changes no walked label leaves it unchanged. If the step is on the host's tag by then, its first tick is Sunday 2026-11-08 06:00Z, the day before the 11-09 run. The timing of the reads is the architect's.

The would-be call is the Desk's record-only `desk.market_only_hold` (addendum 214, #778) on a PASS row of the market-only kind with `would_call` PLAY. Its QB class is the hold's tags (QB-flagged half units / QB unread half units). exec_cohorts: one NFL line, by QB class and exec cell, notional at the would-be units at `desk.exec.cost`, outside every PLAY cell, the n=30 counter and the pooled line; its tail is #446's count (PLAY + would-be, labelled, closing runs from the hold of 2026-10-11). An unread registry prints the line, labelled "certification not read". After a certification the line keeps printing while a would-be row or a #446 row is there (whether "certified" should also remove the history is the architect's to say; as built it does not).

**2026-11-02 — FIXED (ARCHITECT 2026-11-02 16:35 ET, addendum 222 item 2): #798, nfl-v2-gate's reservation gets the two edges #797 fixed for ncaa-gate, in #797's shape; a harness fix before nfl-elo-v2's one run (2026-11-06). No bar, stream or reservation semantics move; `--preflight` is byte-identical.**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "#798 (the same two edges in nfl-v2-gate: a non-EEXIST create error escaping as a traceback; the half-written file's removal not made durable) — RULED: fix in #797's shape, its own small PR after #797 merges so the two harnesses read the same, merged before the 11-06 run; one review round at most under the stop rule. The `needs-ruling` label drops with this."
- **The finding (#798, from Codex's round-1 review of #797):** `reserve()` caught only `FileExistsError` at the exclusive create, so ENOSPC, EACCES or EIO there escaped as a traceback (nothing created, so the read was not spent; only a less clear exit). After a failed write, `os.unlink` was not followed by a directory fsync while the refusal said "the read is not spent"; after a crash before the directory was flushed, the partial file could return and read as a spent run. No incident is known.
- **The fix:** any `OSError` at the create other than `FileExistsError` refuses ("could not be created (...); nothing written, nothing scored, the read is not spent"). After the cleanup the directory is fsynced in both outcomes (our unlink removed the file, or it was already gone). If that fsync fails, the refusal says the removal could not be made durable, names the file to check before the run, and ends "nothing scored", never "the read is not spent". The messages match #797's wording, so the two harnesses read the same.
- **Pinned unchanged:** the success bytes equal main's reserve() (a test runs it beside the new one); the newline stays "\n" (no earlier text-mode bytes to match); `nfl-v2-gate --preflight`'s console is byte-identical against origin/main 212398ea's module on the synthetic stream (three cases); `nfl-backtest`'s golden output passes. Nothing on the roadmap moves.
- **Tracked:** Issue #798 (closed by this PR); tests/test_nfl_v2_reserve_798.py and tests/test_nfl_v2_gate.py.

**2026-11-02 — FIXED (ARCHITECT 2026-11-02 15:55 ET, addendum 221 item 1): #794, ncaa-gate's reservation is written whole or not at all, the shape #784 got for nfl-v2-gate; a harness fix before ncaa-elo-v2's one run (2026-11-09). No bar, stream or reservation semantics move; `--preflight` is byte-identical.**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "#794 — RULED: fix it, the same shape #784 got for nfl-v2-gate (the reservation written whole or not at all; a write failure leaves nothing and the run is not spent; a refusal records nothing), with its tests, in its own small PR that takes the slot #796 frees NOW — ahead of the two addendum-220 PRs still building, because it protects a model lane's one run (ncaa-elo-v2, 2026-11-09) and the leagues' and PL's records can wait an hour. It is a harness fix, not a criterion: the gate's bar, stream and reservation semantics are unchanged; `ncaa-gate --preflight`'s output stays byte-identical (a test pins it). Merged before 11-09 by my block; nothing on the roadmap moves. The `needs-ruling` label drops with this."
- **The finding (#794):** `reserve()` created `<eid>.started.json` with an exclusive create and then wrote it with `json.dump` into `os.fdopen`, with no cleanup. If serialisation, the write or the close failed (a full disk, a value that cannot be serialised), an empty or partial file stayed behind. `declared_unrun()` and `_reserved_why()` read that file as a spent run, so the one read was consumed with no game scored. No incident is known.
- **The fix:** the body is serialised before the exclusive create. After the create it is written whole, fsynced and closed, and the directory is fsynced. Any failure closes the fd, removes our own file and refuses (exit 2: nothing scored, the read is not spent). A failed removal refuses with INSPECT THE FILE. A KeyboardInterrupt is cleaned up and re-raised. Both declarations share the function (ncaa-elo-v1r, ncaa-elo-v2). The helpers mirror nfl_v2_gate's, so no cross-sport import is added.
- **Pinned unchanged:** the success bytes equal the pre-fix implementation's (a test runs the old function beside the new one); `ncaa-gate --preflight`'s console is byte-identical for both ids against origin/main 212398ea's module (golden captured from it). Nothing on the roadmap moves.
- **Tracked:** Issue #794 (closed by this PR); tests/test_ncaa_reserve_794.py.
- **Review on #797 (round 1, three P2s, fixed):** (1) an exclusive create failing with ENOSPC, EACCES or EIO now refuses like the rest (exit 2, nothing created, the read not spent) instead of escaping as an error; (2) after removing a half-written file, the directory is fsynced so the removal is durable, and if that fsync fails the refusal says the file may return after a restart and does not claim the read unspent; (3) the newline is os.linesep, which is what the old text-mode write put on disk (CRLF on Windows), so the success bytes match on every platform. Tests: 32 (12 fail on the round-0 code).
- **Addendum 222 item 1 (ARCHITECT 2026-11-02 16:35 ET), verbatim:** "#797 (#794, ncaa-gate's reservation) — the round-two P2 (fsync the directory in the already-gone branch too) RIDES THIS PR: gate-harness code, two lines, the same class as the fix, the run is 11-09. The ruling's push, no new review round; CI green, then my merge block on the new head." Built: the directory fsync runs after the cleanup in both outcomes (removed by us, or already gone); its failure is said and the refusal then ends "nothing scored". Test: a file another process removed mid-failure (2 cases).

**2026-11-02 — RECEIPT (ARCHITECT 2026-11-02 10:50 ET, addendum 216 item 1(b); item 7's first PR): v22's normalisation finding pinned on the REAL code, read-only. The review's league reproduces exactly through the real code: 3.000 goals in, 2.739407407407407 out (−8.6864%) at b = 1.2 with n = 40 shrinkage. The addendum's "about −8% at b = 1.15" is the pre-shrinkage average-team figure: 0.925 per rating, 3.000 in and 2.759 out (−8.02%), a home/away ratio of 1.15 against the data's 1.353. v22 does not move; no bar moves; no output changes.**
- **Ruling (verbatim, all items):**
> ARCHITECT 2026-11-02 10:50 ET — addendum 216: the external review of v22 (the operator's GPT, 2026-11-02, with its normalisation_diagnostic.py) — read against the code (law 1, by me) and ruled. v22 does not move; the pl-availability shadow is untouched; the findings go to the successor candidate and to the ledger.
>
> 1. THE NORMALISATION FINDING — CONFIRMED in the real code, not only in the review's reimplementation. src/walters/training.py builds the context per competition as g = total goals / (2 × matches) and b = home mean / g (clamped to [1.0, 1.30]); src/models/poisson.py estimate_strengths deflates HOME goals by b before averaging and divides BOTH averages by the undeflated g; the forecast is home λ = g·b·A_H·D_A·elo and away λ = g·A_A·D_H·elo. For a league of average teams the deflated per-team average is g·(3−b)/2, not g, so every average rating reads (3−b)/2 (0.925 at the default b = 1.15, before shrinkage), the forecast total reads g·(1+b)·((3−b)/2)² (about −8% at b = 1.15) and the home/away goal ratio the model expresses is b where the data's is b/(2−b) (1.15 against 1.35). The review's synthetic counterexample (3.000 in, 2.739 out) reproduces exactly from these lines. It is a structural bias toward fewer goals and away/draw mass, not a bug in a branch; it passed through v22's gate because the gate measures v22 against its bar, not its equations against themselves. RULED: (a) a FINDING Issue (model, finding, sport:soccer, M) with the equations above and the review cited; (b) Code's receipt PR, read-only: one test that drives the REAL estimate_strengths and the real forecast with the review's synthetic league and pins the −8.7% total (the review's script is the receipt's citation, not repository code — it reimplements the equations), plus a read-only line that evaluates the same expressions on the production model's stored PL context (g and b as stored) and prints the implied average-team rating, total and home/away ratio; posted on the Issue; (c) NO change to v22: the fix is a candidate through the frozen gate, never a patch to a live model.
>
> 2. THE 30-MATCH SWITCH — CONFIRMED as a discontinuity (the current-season window drops the supplementary history at the league's 30th finished match regardless of a team's own games), and the soccer backtest's default skip of the first 40 matches means that boundary has never been evaluated. RULED: a LIMITATION Issue (model, limitation, sport:soccer, S) for the unevaluated boundary; the per-team continuity (a weight on each team's own usable exposure between its prior-season estimate and its current-season evidence, promoted clubs as a persistent prior) is a DESIGN ELEMENT of the successor candidate of item 3, not a change to v22 and not a reopening of the rejected time-decay experiment.
>
> 3. THE SUCCESSOR — #656 is the vehicle, dated now (the model lanes come first; the PL is the only live model-edge family today, and v22 reads behind the close over the rolling 30): a jointly fitted log-linear model log λ_H = μ + h + α_H + δ_A + β·ΔE, log λ_A = μ + α_A + δ_H − β·ΔE, with identification constraints and regularisation, the Dixon–Coles correction kept, the per-team continuity of item 2 built in — the baseline, the home effect, attack, defence and Elo's increment estimated coherently so item 1's inconsistency cannot exist by construction. Roadmap lane "soccer-v23" (Issue #656): 11-13 code — the design PR (the fit, its constraints, the early-season treatment, the harness: one run at the frozen soccer gate on the frozen pot, the reservation pattern); 11-20 architect — the declaration with the bar written before any result: the pot's log-loss below v22's by at least 0.0050, a tie a rejection (the improve bar as it stands), with the early-season matches INCLUDED in the scored set (no 40-match skip for this candidate: its own declared window states the skip, and it is zero); 11-27 operator — the one run on my word, my block, on a .backup copy opened immutable=1; PASS → a 60-game prospective shadow on the host's PL pages beside v22 (the pl-availability pattern, its own window counted from its first host page), the read by me; earliest_live the day after that read. No date moves a bar.
>
> 4. BACKTEST-TO-PRODUCTION PARITY — ACCEPTED as a lane, not a build today: #425 already records the injury factor's absence from v22's gate; the review's inventory (the scoring context, the Elo state, the early-season history and the match factors differ between soccer_backtest and _generate_predictions_soccer) becomes a LIMITATION Issue (model, limitation, sport:soccer, M) with that table; the engineering direction — ONE prediction function taking a versioned, immutable input snapshot, invoked by replay and by live alike, "same model, same inputs at the same instant, same probabilities" as the acceptance test — is a lane (track:model, class:lane, size:L, no date) to be designed with the soccer-v23 harness so the successor is testable where v22 was not. Historical injuries are never manufactured; the sealed availability window is never read early.
>
> 5. THE AVAILABILITY EXPERIMENT — untouched, as the review itself says. The two latent limitations it names (a defender's or goalkeeper's absence expressed as the team's own attack; the injury × missing-regular × XI-strength overlap when lineups are on) are recorded as LIMITATION Issues (model, limitation, sport:soccer, S each) for a later replacement-aware availability candidate with no date, after pl-availability-v1's read.

The review's synthetic counterexample (3.000 in, 2.739 out) reproduces exactly from these lines. It is a structural bias toward fewer goals and away/draw mass, not a bug in a branch; it passed through v22's gate because the gate measures v22 against its bar, not its equations against themselves.
